planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall; this classic van der Steen selection is the parent of the Chick Charms series cultivar 'Berry Bomb'.

directions: Director Jacobs forms a cupped, cilia-fringed rosette 3-4 inches across whose long white hairs along the leaf margins give it a frosted appearance, while the leaf color itself glows deep burgundy red through spring and summer before softening to pink, green, and gray tones in cooler weather. One of the most cold-hardy Sempervivum cultivars in wide circulation, it tolerates winters into zone 3 without protection and is far more likely to be lost to soggy soil than to frost. Grow in lean, gravelly, sharply drained soil in full sun, where strong light intensifies the red pigment that fades in shade. Propagate by separating the offsets ('chicks') that form readily on short stolons around the mother rosette.

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, fast-draining gritty soil in full sun in spring or fall; this long-cultivated tectorum selection has been grown in gardens since at least the early twentieth century.

directions: 'Atroviolaceum' is an old Sempervivum tectorum selection forming large, open rosettes whose green leaf bases shift into a rich reddish-violet flush across the blade, deepening further with bright sun and cold weather. Like other tectorum forms it is exceptionally cold hardy, shrugging off winters into zone 3 unprotected, and succumbs to wet, poorly drained soil long before it succumbs to frost. Grow in lean, gritty, sharply drained soil in full sun to keep the rosettes tight and richly colored. Established clumps spread readily by offsets, which can be detached once rooted and replanted to increase stock.

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, sharply drained gravelly soil in full sun in spring or fall; outdoor sun exposure is needed to bring out the fiery color.

directions: Red Devil carries fiery red rosettes accented with shifting splashes of pink and orange that intensify through the seasons, holding their color best when grown outdoors in full sun rather than in shaded containers. Like other sempervivums it is thoroughly cold hardy, happily overwintering under an insulating blanket of snow, and is far more vulnerable to waterlogged soil than to freezing temperatures. Grow in lean, sharply drained gravelly or gritty soil, since standing moisture around the crown causes rot. It multiplies by offsets on short stolons, which can be separated and replanted to form new colonies.

planting.note: Press offsets onto the surface of lean, fast-draining gritty soil in full sun in spring or fall; this hybrid of unknown parentage forms unusually small, densely matting rosettes.

directions: Silver King forms small, silvery-tinged, minty green rosettes only about an inch across, producing short-stalked offsets that quickly build into crowded, richly textured mats. Leaf color intensifies in cold weather, when strong red-purple centers contrast boldly against frost and snow, and the species-typical hardiness carries it through winters into zone 4 without protection. Grow in lean, sharply drained, gritty soil in full sun, since excess moisture around the crown is a far greater threat than cold. Older rosettes send up a thin flowering stalk topped with small pink flowers in summer and then die, but the spreading mat of offsets continues on; propagate by separating rooted offsets.

planting.note: Plant stem or rosette cuttings in well-drained, lean, gritty soil in full sun to light shade; aeoniums are winter-growing, summer-dormant succulents and establish best when rooted during the cooler growing season.

directions: 'Luteovariegatum' is a variegated sport of the tree aeonium bearing broad rosettes striped in green and creamy yellow, with leaf tips often blushing pink to red in bright light, carried atop slender, woody stems that lengthen with age. Like other Aeonium arboreum forms it follows a winter-growing, summer-dormant rhythm and is tender, needing container culture or winter protection outside the mildest near-frost-free climates. Grow in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade, giving afternoon shade in hot-summer regions to prevent leaf scorch and keep the variegation crisp. Because variegated seedlings do not come true, propagate only from stem or rosette cuttings, which callous and root readily.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America

planting.note: Separate offsets from established rosettes and pot in well-drained cactus mix; this selection was chosen over successive generations for unusually wide, bright white leaf banding.

directions: Super White is a selection of the familiar zebra haworthia chosen for notably broader, more brightly white raised bands across its dark green, triangular leaves, giving an even stronger striped effect than standard attenuata. Like the species, it is naturally adapted to growing in dappled shade under shrubs and rock overhangs in South Africa's Eastern Cape, making it tolerant of low light and an excellent indoor succulent for a bright but indirect windowsill. Grow in well-drained cactus or succulent mix, watering only once the soil has dried and withholding water further in winter. It offsets readily into multi-rosette clumps that can be divided to propagate new plants.

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in well-drained, lean, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light; this variegated Echeveria elegans sport needs bright light to maintain its pastel color.

directions: Blue Surprise is a variegated sport of the Mexican snowball with a neat rosette that shifts between pale silver, powder blue, and pink, the pink intensifying under bright sun and dry conditions; the pastel cast comes from a coat of farina, a protective powdery wax typical of many echeverias. It is tender and will not tolerate hard frost, needing container culture and a bright windowsill or grow light indoors wherever winters dip below freezing. Grow in well-drained, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix in full sun to bright light, letting the soil dry fully between waterings since overwatering causes crown rot. As a variegated selection it does not come true from seed, so propagate from leaf cuttings or by separating basal offsets.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America

planting.note: Pot offsets in a fast-draining succulent mix and grow in bright indirect light or light shade, protecting from direct hot midday sun.

directions: Black Beauty is a selection of Gasteria batesiana chosen for exceptionally dark, nearly blackish-green leaves covered in raised, wart-like tubercles, giving an even more dramatic, rugged texture than the typical species form. Native to the dappled shade of South Africa's Great Fish River valley, it thrives in bright indirect light or light shade rather than harsh direct sun, which can scorch its thick leaves. Plant in a fast-draining succulent mix and water only once the soil has dried out fully, cutting back further in winter. It slowly forms small offsetting clumps that can be divided once they crowd their pot, and with good care a single plant can persist for many years.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America

planting.note: Root offsets or leaf cuttings in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light; this Charles Uhl hybrid of Graptopetalum amethystinum and Echeveria purpusorum does not come true from seed.

directions: 'Amethorum' is an intergeneric hybrid between Graptopetalum amethystinum and Echeveria purpusorum, combining a thick, powdery, lavender-grey to dusty-purple leaf color with a compact, tightly packed rosette form inherited from both parents. Strong, unfiltered sun and cool nights deepen the purple-amethyst tones, while shaded plants fade toward a plainer grey-green, so bright light gives the best display. Grow in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix in full sun to bright light, letting the soil dry completely between waterings since the thick, powdery leaves are prone to rot in soggy conditions. It offsets readily at the base and also grows new plants from cleanly detached leaves, making it easy to multiply by cuttings alone.
